chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Opening Music Town in 1942 with Austin McCoy
summary: Spikes and Hollywood McCoy, a student of Johnny's, opened Music Town at Jefferson and Normandie in 1942.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Nobody seems to know whatever happened to Sheffield's pictures. They would be a great document of all the activities of that era. But then Sheffield shows up again...at Music Town, which you opened in what year?
'42, and that was at Jefferson and Normandie, and Music Town was an arts center. I mean, you...I have the program here which you loaned me from one of the...
Yeah, we had a art show there for...a week, I think.

This is the program for "An American Rhapsody," an you've got the Music Town staff pictured in here, and there's B.F. "Reb" Spikes, lyricist; Austin L. McCoy, composer, teacher and arranger, and it was you and Austin McCoy that opened Music Town, right?
Yeah. Austin McCoy was one of my brother's scholars. He took him when he was fifteen, sixteen years old, and he's a...he's still good.

Oh, yeah. He's teaching music and stuff in Compton College out there somewhere, I think. He...we...I call him sometime. Since my eyes are gettin' bad, when I get a idea or somethin', I call him and he comes over and writes it for me.
And he was...he played piano. Is that right?
And you said he was known as "Hollywood" McCoy.
"Hollywood" McCoy. I think he was the first colored boy born out there. He was born out there--'13, I think, '12 or '13. 'Course there might have been more but they say...they say that... you know.
